title: Great Moravia
capsule: Great Moravia (c. 833–907) was the first major political unit of the western Slavs, founded when Mojmír I united Moravia and Nitra around 833 and expelled Pribina of Nitra. Its cultural zenith came under Rastislav (r. 846–870), who invited the Byzantine missionaries Cyril and Methodius in 863; they devised the Glagolitic script and Old Church Slavonic liturgy, foundational to Slavic literacy. Under Svatopluk I (r. 871–894) the realm expanded to encompass Bohemia, Pannonia, and parts of Lesser Poland, becoming the dominant power in Central Europe. After Svatopluk's death internecine strife between his sons fatally weakened the state, and Magyar raids culminating in the Battle of Pressburg (907) dissolved it; its ecclesiastical and cultural legacy persisted in Bohemia and among South Slavs.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The polity's territorial extent is moderately attested through Frankish annals and archaeology at Mikulčice/Staré Město; its outer frontiers, especially in Pannonia and Silesia, are debated and differ across historiographic traditions.
